headline: Raining Cats and Sheds: Seattle Prepares for Rain-Fueled Evacuations
deck: As persistent rain triggers evacuations, Seattle's architectural headwear becomes an unlikely lifeline.
article:
SEATTLE - Persistent downpours have activated the city's full evacuation protocol, complete with pre-approved hat blueprints filed at the assessor's office. Residents now treat their headgear as certified flotation devices rather than fashion statements.

Designs undergo strict review for load-bearing capacity and gutter functionality before any resident can step outside. Rejected submissions leave owners scrambling for last-minute reinforcements.

Evacuation corridors receive mandatory awning checks every 1.8 miles by rain marshals who verify tether strength and clearance. Failure means rerouting entire groups mid-stride.

Automated messages assign each household to a strip-mall shelter pod according to the prior year's HOA precipitation count. The system treats routine rainfall with the same paperwork intensity once reserved for actual disasters.
author: John Doe, Multiverse Gazette Correspondent

oped.title: Evacuations Are for Soft Skulls: Reinforce Your Roof or Get Out
oped.author: Dr. Cornelius Brimstone, Certified Cranial Architect and Founder of Brimstone’s Indestructible Shed-Hat Syndicate
oped.body: Seattle’s latest tantrum over rain merely proves that weak-minded citizens refuse to upgrade their personal architecture. These so-called evacuations could be avoided if every resident simply replaced their flimsy fedoras with my patented forty-pound cast-iron shed models, complete with working gutters and optional chimney. Instead, people whine about neck strain and visibility while my superior product sits on the shelf. The real crisis is not water but ingratitude toward true innovators like myself, whose designs have kept my own household dry since 2019. Blaming the weather is childish; blaming inadequate headwear is accurate. If a few citizens must remain behind because their current hats lack proper load-bearing beams, that is simply natural selection in action. My competitors’ lightweight nonsense has no place in 2026.

classifieds.text: Priced to move before the next deluge: one slightly waterlogged family-sized fedora-home with skylight brim and built-in drainage gutters. Must evacuate by Friday—cash or crypto only.
Urgent: seeking structural milliner to reinforce 200+ residential bowlers ahead of tonight’s shed-storm. Experience with load-bearing feathers a plus; overtime paid in dry socks.
To the residents of Block 47: your oversized cloche shelters are now officially condemned as evacuation rafts. Please vacate by 6 p.m. or be cited for illegal flotation.
Apologies to the couple whose beanie-boat I commandeered during the 3 a.m. downpour—your hat is safe on the roof of the old library. DM for retrieval instructions and possible shared custody.

stories.headline: Hat Conglomerate Announces Rain-Proof Subdivision Units
stories.deck: Stock rises as models double as emergency housing.
stories.article:
The nation's largest architectural hat manufacturer reported a 340 percent increase in custom commissions following Seattle's latest rain warnings. Executives attributed the surge to homeowners requesting expandable brim structures capable of sheltering entire families during prolonged downpours.

Analysts noted that traditional real estate developers have begun partnering with millinery firms to convert suburban lots into hybrid living spaces where the primary residence is worn rather than occupied. One prototype includes a detachable garage section that clips onto the crown.
